limitations.text: The installed Codex CLI v0.157.1 loads AGENTS.md bytes as instruction text and does not implement an @file import in that loader. An agent may choose to read a referenced path, but automatic expansion is not provided by this code. Discovery documentation: https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md; original source: agents_md.rs:150-176,314-322.

RTK's own installer writes the problematic reference: src/hooks/init.rs:3040-3061 constructs an absolute @path globally or @RTK.md locally, then patches AGENTS.md and hooks.json; :4161-4163 formats the @path. Its comment incorrectly assumes Codex resolves such imports. Combined with Codex's loader, this is an inferred upstream RTK instruction-integration defect, not a locally invented reference format.
The inherited instructions-only form already existed in v0.49.0: run_codex_mode_with_paths wrote RTK.md and its @ reference without a Codex hook. Source: src/hooks/init.rs:2647-2681.

The authoritative shared hook gate is src/hooks/decision.rs:38-56,76-96, not a blanket simple-command restriction in hook_cmd.rs. It deliberately refuses rewriting when contains_unattestable_construct is true; all hook integrations share this gate. This is an upstream permission-preserving design limitation.

src/discover/lexer.rs:363-414 rejects executable backticks, $(...) and process substitution, plus file-target redirection. Single-quoted literal substitution text is exempt; fd duplication/closing and /dev/null redirects have exceptions. Subshell grouping and separators are handled separately, not universally rejected here.

src/discover/registry.rs:703-735 rejects heredocs and arithmetic substitution, but dispatches multiline commands to a rewriter; :951-1018 permits safe multiline blocks and refuses unsafe constructs. :1226-1244 handles &&, ||, ; and pipelines, while rejecting pipelines with opaque grouping; :1087-1153 and :1753-1766 apply pipeline safety rules. Therefore pipes, chains and multiple lines are not universal bypass conditions. Neither another hook mode nor --ultra-compact removes these shared gates.

Codex rewriting requires protocol permissionDecision=allow for updatedInput. Native approval and sandbox checks still apply to the rewritten command, but upstream warns that Codex's command classifier does not unwrap rtk, affecting prompts and classification signals. Source: src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs:900-912.

RTK processes selected CLI output, not every context source; proxy deliberately returns unfiltered output. Reductions of command output do not establish provider-token savings or byte-for-byte fidelity.

official_baseline_claims.claim: QMD describes an on-device Markdown search engine combining BM25 full-text retrieval, vector search and LLM reranking through local node-llama-cpp/GGUF models. CLI lexical search is a distinct path from the complete model-backed pipeline; this capability claim does not establish a fixed percentage of token savings.

Upstream supplies structured --json/--files output and MCP query, get, multi_get and status tools for agents; selected line ranges can be retrieved using get's path:from:count form. Savings depend on retrieving the correct bounded source and accounting for both search and fetched content.

limitations.text: Retrieval is limited to configured collections and indexed files. Semantic retrieval requires embeddings; plain query automatically expands through a model, and reranking defaults on. For a deliberately lexical MCP call use typed lex searches with rerank:false; status/get and CLI search do not by themselves establish semantic readiness or token savings.

Issue #991, still open when rechecked, reports that update leaves old content searchable when an indexed file becomes empty or whitespace-only. full-save/cur/qmd/record.json records an isolated reproduction on pinned 2.8.3, beyond the issue's main-branch reproduction; that is prior local synthetic evidence, not a new reproduction in this review.

Issue #989, still open when rechecked, reports that update deactivates every document in a missing collection root while reporting success; cleanup can subsequently remove inactive data. full-save/cur/qmd/record.json records the same failure on an isolated 2.8.3 fixture; ordinary exit success is therefore insufficient as a freshness check.

Issue #971 reports a 2.8.3 stdio race where a model-free status/get request concurrent with model loading can send its JSON-RPC response to stderr and leave the client waiting. It was also reproduced upstream in CPU mode; this review has not reproduced it locally.

Issue #942 reports independent model loads across concurrent 2.8.3 invocations exhausting CPU-host RAM. Separate MCP clients do not automatically share their model processes; this matters if agents invoke expansion or reranking despite the lexical catalog's lack of vectors.

Issue #997 reports that MCP/bench can bypass the project-local custom-model trust gate. Our explicit --index selection bypasses project-local config discovery, as confirmed in tagged src/cli/qmd.ts, so this is not an observed failure of our named-index registration; replacing it with the plugin's bare qmd mcp command would remove that scope safeguard.

official_baseline_claims.claim: Upstream advertises 61% less context, 84% fewer tool calls and 37x faster exploration than grep-based exploration in its VS Code benchmark, using Claude Opus 4.6 on a 2.45-million-line codebase. These are upstream task/benchmark claims, not a 1.14.0-to-1.15.0 comparison, our stack's results, or provider-billing savings.

Search combines dense semantic retrieval and BM25 with reciprocal-rank fusion, and the default auto watcher refreshes an indexed project. The server also exposes dependency/symbol graphs and searchable context artifacts; these are retrieval capabilities rather than a native token-savings counter.

limitations.text: Indexing is asynchronous; check codebase_status and search after indexing completes. codebase_status reports index progress/state and chunk counts, not saved tokens; search results still need checking against the original source.

Coverage depends on indexing scope and ignore rules. Dot-files and dot-directories are excluded by default, so a search miss is not evidence that a hidden configuration or agent definition does not exist.

Watcher/manual/off settings determine freshness: disabling the watcher and startup recovery deliberately leaves a snapshot requiring explicit codebase_update. Branch indexes are shared by default; branch-aware indexing is opt-in and an explicit project ID overrides branch separation.

Embedding and vector-storage services are prerequisites, not provided by a bare MCP registration. The default uses local Ollama and Qdrant; alternate endpoints require compatible embedding dimensions/model configuration. This does not route Claude/Codex generation traffic or prove prompt-cache savings.

The Claude plugin's duplicate-registration notice is a SessionStart hook; it does not intercept arbitrary reads or compress every tool result. MCP-only adoption does not automatically install the plugin's agent/skill instructions.

limitations.text: Static HTTP MCP cannot correlate a tool call with a lifecycle-hook session ID. Static clients must pass exact workspace and project together; auto_scope=per_session alone does not fix a static entry. Claude's optional stdio bridge forwards a native session ID but has documented /clear/resume limits.

Open issue #930 reports that explicit project-scoped queries, which static clients require, omit the _global preference union. Do not remove project scope or silently search all projects to recover mandatory instructions; retain those instructions in native project/user instruction files.

Open issue #932 reports cross-project Claude subagent activity attributed to the parent project's cwd/session. Explicit MCP recall scope cannot repair already misattributed hook capture; the report's workaround is a real native session rooted in each target project. This is an upstream report, not a reproduction performed in this review.

Open issue #929 reports stale search entries after direct wiki-file deletion and missing embeddings after direct rewrites until embed runs. It also notes that --data-dir alone does not redirect thin-client commands away from the default server; specify the intended server URL when qualifying an isolated store.

The tagged renderer defines nine Claude events but seven Codex events; the Codex set has no SubagentStart or SubagentStop. Complete Codex child lifecycle capture/finalization is therefore not established by matching the seven configured top-level events.

Memory scopes are organizational routing, not project authorization boundaries; upstream describes a single-tenant trust model. Captured observations and retrieved text must be treated as data, and native sign-ins/model routes remain separate from memory service configuration.

Issue #920 remains an open RFC proposing reduced MCP tool-description/schema/response overhead. Its operator-reported size estimate is not a shipped optimization or proof that every client pays that many uncached billed tokens every turn.

The pinned MCP memory_query declaration has no read-only tool annotation. Our retained restricted-Codex experiment, and this worker's attempted scoped query, received an approval-required denial under approval_policy=never; a configured HTTP server therefore does not guarantee recall in every sandbox. Native evidence: rr/ai-memory/records.json, ai-memory-d3-codex-exec and ai-memory-e2-codex-exec.

MarkItDown converts supported documents to Markdown for text-analysis and LLM workflows, aiming to retain useful headings, lists, tables and links. Supported format families include HTML, PDF, Office, text, archives and media, with dependencies varying by format.
Upstream documents Python 3.10 through 3.14, isolated environments, an all-extras pip installation and selective format extras such as pdf, docx and pptx.
The CLI accepts filenames or stdin and can write Markdown with -o; the Python library exposes conversion methods. Third-party plugins are disabled by default.
The separate markitdown-mcp package publishes convert_to_markdown(uri), with STDIO as the default transport and optional Streamable HTTP/SSE. Its client-specific example targets Claude Desktop.

The release already includes charset, CSV, document-format and URI fixes, underline/strikethrough and image-source handling changes, an MCP SDK migration and an OCR refactor. These are already within the current pin, not an outstanding upgrade.

The optional OCR plugin uses configured llm_client/llm_model objects and vision inference; the Python API example enables plugins explicitly. Without an llm_client, its documentation says OCR is skipped.

limitations.text: Upstream positions the output for text analysis and explicitly warns that it may not suit high-fidelity document presentation. Format support in the README does not mean a base installation contains every format dependency.
Conversion performs I/O with the current process's privileges. Upstream recommends narrow conversion entry points for the required input type and input sanitization where inputs are untrusted.

The MCP package is intended for local trusted use; its HTTP/SSE examples bind to localhost and its security section says it has no authentication. This companion package is a separate deployment from the CLI.

The released HTTP URI path calls requests-session get(uri, stream=True) without an explicit timeout, and response conversion buffers content. This source behavior limits unattended URL handling without external bounds.
ZIP conversion reads decompressed entries into memory before nested conversion; the inspected converter does not impose an expanded-size budget.

The OCR README's --llm-client/--llm-model CLI example does not match the released CLI parser, which defines neither flag. Use its published Python API example for qualification instead. Conflicting example: https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/blob/v0.1.8/packages/markitdown-ocr/README.md#L33

limitations.text: npm installs require Node 24 or newer. The package's CLI/runtime and optional native standalone distributions are distinct installation choices.

File-backed string arguments are supported as key=@path or --key @path; @@ escapes a literal leading @. --args/--params accept a JSON object, and source also supports --args - for JSON read from stdin (https://github.com/openclaw/mcporter/blob/v0.14.1/src/cli/call-arguments.ts#L317). This is a named UTF-8 string facility, not arbitrary binary attachment transport.

In v0.14.1, resolveSelectorAndTool at src/cli/call-arguments.ts:170-171 consumes the first positional token when no --server or expression-provided server is present, even if --tool was supplied; trailing named arguments are parsed afterward. A call must select the target unambiguously before relying on content=@file to reach a required content property. The same source handles --args - at :317-322 and reads @path at :362-386.
The optional mcporter serve MCP bridge exposes only configured keep-alive servers; it is not an automatic interception layer for every MCP connection made by Claude or Codex.
